extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration attorneys, policy stakeholders, and members of the public interested in H-1B rulemakings and notice-and-comment submissions
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing of rules, proposed rules, notices, and other documents related to the H-1B program, summarizing regulatory requirements, proposed changes, eligibility conditions, fees, and procedural information relevant to H-1B petitions and registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection process objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a weighted selection process that will generally favor the allocation of H-1B visas to higher-skilled and higher-paid aliens, while maintaining the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through this rule DHS intends to favor higher-skilled/higher-paid beneficiaries but still preserve access across wage levels; the approach is intended to better serve congressional intent and disincentivize abuse of the H-1B program to fill relatively lower-paid, lower-skilled positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary‑centric selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a beneficiary-centric selection process for H-1B registrations for unique beneficiaries for filing of H-1B cap‑subject petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selection approach shifts emphasis toward individual beneficiaries (versus employer-centric processes); related integrity measures accompany this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date flexibility for cap‑subject petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide flexibility on the employment start date listed on H-1B cap‑subject petitions in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits some adjustment to the start date to accommodate legitimate workforce needs or administrative timing; flexibility is narrowly scoped and constrained by regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity measures for H‑1B registration and program abuse prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement additional integrity measures related to the H-1B registration process and program integrity to reduce misuse and fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited include bolstering the registration process, new site-visit requirements, measures to limit multiple registrations by related entities, and tools to deter use of the program to fill lower‑paid/lower‑skilled positions or to outsource U.S. jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9-11 Biometric Entry‑Exit Fee applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Require covered employers to submit the 9-11 Biometric Entry‑Exit Fee for all extension‑of‑stay petitions, regardless of whether a Fraud Fee applies; the fee continues to apply unchanged to petitions seeking an initial grant of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency interprets ambiguous statutory language to include extension‑of‑stay petitions that do not involve a change of employer; the rule would increase the share of H-1B petitions subject to the biometric fee (example: an analysis showing share rising from 29% to 84% under the proposed rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer attestations required for LCAs (INA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers seeking to use H-1B, H-1B1, or E-3 nonimmigrants must make certain attestations to the Secretary of Labor as mandated by the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) before admission to perform work in a specialty occupation or as a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory attestations are implemented in DOL and DHS regulations (20 CFR part 655, subparts H and I; 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)). The forms and instructions (e.g., ETA-9035/9035E) operationalize the attestations and recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing wage computation and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise computation of prevailing wage levels under the Department's four‑tiered prevailing wage structure using the OEWS wage survey to better align prevailing wages with wages paid to U.S. workers in the occupation and area of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed revisions aim to reduce incentives for employers to use programs to replace U.S. workers with lower‑paid foreign workers and to strengthen program integrity; changes apply across PERM and H‑1B/H‑1B1/E‑3 contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot program domestic visa renewal eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for the pilot program to resume domestic H-1B visa renewals requires that applicants (examples extracted): not have a visa ineligibility requiring a waiver; have an approved and unexpired H-1B petition; have been most recently admitted in H-1B status; be currently maintaining H-1B status; have a period of authorized admission in H-1B status that has not expired; and intend to reenter the United States in H-1B status after a temporary period abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some requirements derive from statute/regulation; others are discretionary. The Federal Register notice lists the numbered eligibility items to determine participation in the pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for filing H‑1B cap‑subject petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners may not file H-1B petitions more than 6 months before the date of actual need for the employee; earliest date for cap allocation filings is April 1 (six months prior to FY start Oct 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constrains when petitioners can submit cap‑subject petitions for a given fiscal year; guidance ties fiscal timing to INA provisions (8 U.S.C. 1184(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on multiple registrations by related entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Address and restrict multiple H-1B electronic registrations submitted by related entities to prevent gaming of the registration system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and final rules reference multiple-registration concerns and propose regulatory language to identify and limit related-party duplicate registrations; part of broader integrity measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'specialty occupation' and 'employer‑employee relationship'
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise regulatory definitions relating to 'specialty occupation' and the 'employer‑employee relationship' (including guidance for beneficiary‑owners and start‑up entrepreneurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes aim to better implement Congressional intent regarding exemptions from the cap for qualifying institutions or entities and to clarify when an employment qualifies as a specialty occupation and the nature of the employer relationship for petition purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS online account functionality and company administration
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS is enhancing registrant account functionality to allow companies to set up company administrator accounts and file Form I‑129 petitions in addition to H‑1B registrations; company administrators can invite members to collaborate and members complete personal profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational and procedural standard for how registrants and employers will use the online system; includes data‑entry and collaboration burdens and anticipated respondent burden under PRA notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: H‑1B Registration Fee treatment in fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative correction: DHS exempted the H‑1B Registration Fee from the $50 online filing discount in the regulatory text; regulatory corrections remove unnecessary paragraphing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical regulatory corrections affect how the registration fee is presented and whether it receives online‑filing discounts; applies to agency fee schedule and form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection and PRA comment/extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: DOL, DHS, and USCIS publish information collection requests (ICRs) for forms related to H‑1B (e.g., LCAs, ETA‑9141, ETA‑9035/9035E, USCIS online account) and solicit public comment and OMB review under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices set out the PRA process, the specific forms or collections under review, OMB control numbers, and invite public comments on burden, need, and content; extensions may be requested without changes or with revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing wage determination application requirements (forms/process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers seeking prevailing wage determinations must submit specified forms (e.g., ETA‑9141 and instructions, Appendix A, ETA 9165 where applicable) and meet the Department's information and retention requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice covers which forms are in scope, the purpose (application for prevailing wage determination), and that action seeks to extend or revise information collections; ties to PERM and temporary programs (H‑1B, H‑2B, etc.).
